chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Uthaymah, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and his wives were with him. He said, 'He smelled the scent of the nathuh (scented water/vinegar mixture) and said, 'What is this?' They said, 'It is nathuh in which the sayyakh (a type of vinegar or scent) is placed.' He said, 'Then he ordered it to be poured out into the balu'ah (a large water vessel or basin).'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah: A common title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الصَّيَّاح: Sayyakh: A specific type of vinegar or aromatic substance mentioned in the context of the mixture.
key_terms.النَّضُوح: Nathuh: A mixture of water and vinegar or scented water, often used for purification or fragrance.
key_terms.الْبَالُوعَة: Al-Balu'ah: A large basin or vessel for water, often used for ritual washing or storing water.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on nathuh and sayyakh in Shia jurisprudence according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) orders the disposal of *sayyakh* (a type of musk or scent) found in his household, reflecting the scholarly debate regarding its ritual purity (*taharah*) versus its status as a pure substance (*mutaharr*). This incident is frequently cited by Shia jurists to discuss the permissibility of using musk in prayer and its classification among the impurities or pure items that may be discarded to avoid doubt (*istishab*). The narrative underscores the Imam’s meticulous attention to ritual purity in domestic settings, linking material objects to their spiritual implications in worship.
